subject: Re: Renewal discussion & capacity surge - TidalWave
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@tidalwave.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-21T15:08:00Z
Subject: Renewal strategy & recent bakeoff

Ben —

Quick note from our side as we start renewal planning. We ran a short bakeoff last week between Redwood and BlueCluster for our customer-facing recommendation engine. BlueCluster came in ~25% cheaper at steady-state token cost and showed a small P95 latency improvement during long tails. Our CTO wants to understand what it would take to stay with Redwood for the next 12 months.

We have an upcoming commercial review on Nov 9 and I need a tangible plan: capacity uplift options, committed pricing, and any performance optimization bets you can make (quantization, dedicated pools, etc.). Can you put together a short proposal and an estimate for a 2x capacity uplift for peak windows?

Alex
Director of ML Platform
TidalWave Labs
(attachment: tidalwave_benchmark_summary.pdf (pdf, 1.2MB) — cook-off metrics and traces)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@tidalwave.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-22T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal strategy & recent bakeoff

Alex — thanks for the heads up and for sharing the benchmark. Appreciate the detail.

Short answer: we can close the gap and protect you from switching risk. High level next steps I propose:
- Immediate: a 30-day capacity bridge (reserved burst pool) to match BlueCluster's peak economics while we finalize long-term terms.
- Within 2 weeks: an on-site benchmark with our performance engineering team to reproduce your workload at scale (we'll bring a tuned quantized candidate if that's okay).
- Commercial: a commit-based overlay for the next 12 months that gives you price protection and guaranteed latency SLOs for priority traffic.

I looped in Marissa from Accounts & Monica from CS to scope commitments. We'll follow up with a concrete XLS and numbers by Monday.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(attachment stub: proposed_capacity_bridge.xlsx)

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@tidalwave.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@tidalwave.com>
Date: 2026-10-22T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal strategy & recent bakeoff

Thanks Ben — that sounds promising. Two clarifications before you finalize numbers: (1) our peak windows are 9pm-11pm PT and 2-3x baseline; (2) our procurement team will need a bridge term no longer than 90 days (they want to avoid open-ended credits).

If you can show parity on cost for the 2x uplift and a documented rollback/fallback plan, I can present a recommendation to our CTO next week.

Alex

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-26T17:31:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal strategy & recent bakeoff

Alex — attaching the proposed bridge plan and a short summary of technical mitigations. Main points:

1) Capacity Bridge (30–90 days configurable)\  - Dedicated reserved burst pool sized to match 2x peak (9pm–11pm PT)\  - Price overlay: 20% blended uplift vs list for bridge period (aimed to match competitor steady-state at your projected utilization)

2) Long-term commit (12 months)\  - Option A: 12-month committed units at 15% below list with a guaranteed CPU/GPU slot reservation (SLA: P95 latency target with credits)\  - Option B: 12-month committed units + performance engineering retainer (quarterly bench) at 20% below list for capacity uplift >2.5x

3) Performance plan\  - On-site benchmark session (Nov 2–4 window) to validate latency at scale; we bring a quantized variant and a tuned kernel set.\  - Prefix/KV cache tuning and workload-aware batching to reduce token cost by 10–18% depending on prompt shape.

4) Rollback & safety\  - Automated routing policy to fallback to a conservative model variant and cross-region spill for peak events.

Attachments: proposed_capacity_bridge.xlsx (capacity by window & pricing), tactical_changes.txt (ops steps)

Would you like me to convert Option A into a tracked SOW and DocuSign link if procurement approves a 60–90 day bridge?

—Ben
(quoted: "On Wed, Oct 21, 2026, Alex Turner wrote:...)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-27T08:44:00Z
Subject: RE: Renewal strategy & recent bakeoff

Ben — reviewed the numbers. We can approve a 60-day bridge at the proposed overlay provided legal signs off on the rollback clause and we attach a modest expansion commitment (2x baseline committed for 12 months). Monica — can you confirm we can staff the Nov 2–4 bench and estimate SRE effort?

Also propose we offer a one-time onboarding credit of $25k in case TidalWave wants to accelerate provisioning for the dedicated pool. That helps procurement justify the bridge.

—Marissa
VP, Strategic Accounts

(Forwarding Ben's proposed_capacity_bridge.xlsx)

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@tidalwave.com>

Subject: Re: Renewal strategy & recent bakeoff

Team — thank you. Procurement and our CTO reviewed internally. The bridge + 12-month commit Option A is acceptable as a recommendation. Two asks before we finalize: (1) please send an SOW and DocuSign link with the 60-day bridge parameters and the 12-month committed units; (2) include the rollback playbook as an appendix so my infra team can sign off.

If we get docs by Monday EOD I will route for signature and we should be able to keep the renewal on the Nov 9 timeline. Appreciated — this was a helpful, pragmatic approach versus a hard-price counter.

Alex Turner
Director of ML Platform
TidalWave Labs
